svg.title: 1 The problem
svg.desc: Section 1, The problem. Federated learning trains a shared model while the data stays where it was produced. In each round, participants send model updates to an aggregator and receive the combined model back. Two guarantees are usually missing. Participants have no way to confirm that the aggregate they receive is correct, and the public-key cryptography that protects the exchange, RSA and elliptic curves, falls to a large quantum computer running Shor's algorithm. Figure 1. One round of federated learning. Updates flow in and the new model flows out, yet nothing in the round proves the aggregate is honest.
